clue.text: The editor sent back excellent piece of writing about sex

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so the abbreviation is read from right to left
about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: ED is the standard abbreviation for editor; 'The' doubles as the definition
fine means very good
'it' is an old euphemism for sex or sex appeal
a newspaper article is a piece of writing

explanation.surface: An editor rejects a fine essay on sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' does double duty: it is both the definition and part of 'The editor'. 'It' as a word for sex or sex appeal is dated slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammarians call the word 'the' the definite article, as opposed to the indefinite 'a'.

clue.text: Pepys is troubled by day with a digestive complaint

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed and thrown out of their order

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for day
the diarist's name and the following word, taken as letters to rearrange
taken as written

explanation.surface: The diarist Samuel Pepys suffers from indigestion during the day.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes before the rearranged letters and A after them; 'by' just places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is the medical term for indigestion, an upset of the stomach after eating.

clue.text: Move swiftly, and perhaps pound boxer

blocks.note: to fly is to move very fast
a pound is an example of a weight, as 'perhaps' signals

explanation.surface: Advice to a boxer: dance quickly and maybe hammer the opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like a verb meaning to hit, as a boxer would, but it is the unit of mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyweight is a boxer in one of the lightest weight classes.

clue.text: Bears down south, south of Nebraska and Arkansas

indicators.note: in a down entry, south of means placed underneath, so the letter follows the states

blocks.note: NE is the US postal code for Nebraska
AR is the US postal code for Arkansas
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Bears are heading down south, below Nebraska and Arkansas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like the animals, but 'bears down' is a verb phrase meaning approaches.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear down on something is to close in on it, which is what something approaching does.

clue.text: Bird one consumed with salt

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird
an means one, as in 'an apple'
consumed food is food that was eaten

explanation.surface: A bird eats something seasoned with salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With salt' reads as seasoning; 'salt' is the chemical sense and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A titanate is a chemical salt formed from titanium dioxide and a metal oxide.

clue.text: Catch a break, say

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the phrase and listen to the result

blocks.note: a break is a rest, and the two words spoken together run into one

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to finally have some luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch a break' is an idiom for getting lucky; split it after 'Catch' to find the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest a criminal is to catch them and take them into custody.

clue.text: The highest sum paid for toll road constructed around capital of Poland

indicators.note: something constructed is built up from parts in a new arrangement
around means the rebuilt letters surround a single letter
a capital is the head of a country's name, signalling its opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the two words as letters to be rearranged
capital means the first letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: A huge fee was paid to build a toll road around the Polish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Poland' tempts you toward Warsaw, but it is just the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Top dollar is an idiom for the highest price someone will pay.

clue.text: Appropriate time to follow chicken home

indicators.note: to follow means come after, so the letter goes at the end

blocks.note: a coop is where hens are kept
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It's the right moment for the hens to go back to their house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as the adjective meaning suitable, but it is the verb meaning to take over.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-opt something is to take it for your own use, which is to appropriate it.

clue.text: Showing keen interest in Stone Age relics

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: the run starts at the end of the first word and ends at the start of the last

explanation.surface: An archaeologist fascinated by prehistoric remains.
explanation.definitionFit: An eager person is enthusiastic and keenly interested in something.

clue.text: Ringleader possibly tidied party mess

indicators.note: tidying a mess puts things into a different order

blocks.note: the two words as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone, perhaps the organiser, cleaned up after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks the definition as an example: the head of a spy ring is a kind of ringleader.
explanation.definitionFit: A spymaster directs a network of agents, so leads a spy ring.

clue.text: A form of rock surrounding northern point

indicators.note: surrounding means one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: prog rock is a style of rock music
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A geology note about a rock formation round a northern headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests geology, but it is the music genre progressive rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is a pointed spike, such as a tine of a fork.

clue.text: Writer‘s sudden appearance I ignored

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: emersion is the act of emerging into view
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer's surprise entrance went unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of EMERSION to get Ralph Waldo Emerson, the American essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a nineteenth-century American essayist and poet.

clue.text: Hit man‘s stomach initially, then nose

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
then means next in sequence, so the second piece follows the first

blocks.note: first letter of the word
hooter is British slang for a nose

explanation.surface: A boxer's punches land first on the belly, then the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit man' reads as a contract killer but a shooter is anyone who fires a gun; hooter is jokey British slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooter is a gunman, and a hired gunman is a hit man.

clue.text: Wisdom shown in story by London, say

blocks.note: a saga is a long story
London is an example of a city

explanation.surface: A wise tale written by Jack London, the author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'London' suggests the novelist Jack London, but it is just an example of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacity is good judgement and shrewdness, a synonym for wisdom.

clue.text: Refuse to move slowly to see bird

blocks.note: chaff is husks and waste, refuse in the sense of rubbish
to inch is to creep along gradually

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher declines to creep closer to a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb meaning decline; it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaffinch is a common European finch with a pink breast.

clue.text: Boy and girl getting tense, resulting in curses

indicators.note: getting means taking something in, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: B is a dictionary abbreviation for boy
lass is a word for a girl
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A couple's argument grows heated and they start swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside LASS, with B in front.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Blast!' is a mild oath, so blasts are curses or exclamations of annoyance.

clue.text: Pasta‘s prepared past eight

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, as ingredients are worked into a new form

blocks.note: the two words as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Dinner was cooked after eight o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a type of pasta made in long thin strands.

clue.text: Conductor‘s rest being disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed things are knocked out of place, so the letters move

blocks.note: the two words as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A conductor's break from rehearsal keeps getting interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' sounds musical, fitting a conductor, but it is just anagram letters.
explanation.definitionFit: William Steinberg was a German-American orchestral conductor who led the Pittsburgh Symphony.

clue.text: Willingness to write song

blocks.note: to pen something is to write it
a chant is a simple song

explanation.surface: Someone is eager to compose music.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a liking or inclination for something, a readiness to do it.

clue.text: Receptacle husband dropped the wrong way

indicators.note: dropped means let go, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: an ashtray is a receptacle for ash
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband drops a container and it falls the wrong way up.
explanation.definitionFit: Astray means off the right path, going in the wrong direction.

clue.text: Contract law protects a society

indicators.note: to protect something is to enclose and shield it

blocks.note: a decree is an official order having the force of law
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Legislation safeguarding a club or association.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a legal noun, fitting law, but it is the verb meaning shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To decrease is to become smaller, which is what something that contracts does.

clue.text: Handbag collection

blocks.note: first meaning: a small strapless bag held in the hand
second meaning: a group, as of eggs or of things

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like a fashion range, but each is a separate meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a strapless evening bag and a group of eggs or items gathered together.

clue.text: Collapse having consumed a fine eastern food item

indicators.note: something that has consumed something holds it inside

blocks.note: to fall is to collapse
taken as written
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: Someone keels over after eating a fancy Middle Eastern dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Falafel is a fried ball of ground chickpeas, a Middle Eastern snack.

clue.text: Batter put in iron mould

indicators.note: put in means placed inside another piece

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
to ram is to batter, as with a battering ram

explanation.surface: Cooking: pour batter into an iron tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' suggests cooking but it is the verb meaning strike hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To frame something is to shape or form it, as a mould does.

clue.text: Drag queen’s 12

blocks.note: to lug is to haul or drag
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to a drag queen, as if naming a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 12 across, a shooter or gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Luger is a German semi-automatic pistol, so a type of shooter.

clue.text: Become entangled, attached to twig

blocks.note: a sleeve can catch on a nail, becoming snagged
on as in fastened on, attached

explanation.surface: Something gets snagged on a small branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twig' looks like a small branch but is informal British slang for understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is to grasp or understand, the same as to catch on.

clue.text: That woman’s appearing in upcoming film, that’s the point

indicators.note: in a down entry upcoming means rising, read from bottom to top
appearing in a film means placed inside it

blocks.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film about an alien
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: An actress stars in a forthcoming film, which is what matters.
explanation.definitionFit: 'There!' is said to clinch an argument, meaning that is exactly the point.

clue.text: Air retains gases, primarily Oxygen, Nitrogen and ___?

definitions.text: Air retains gases, primarily Oxygen, Nitrogen and ___?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take each word's opening letter

blocks.note: opening letters of the three words
opening letters of the two gas names

explanation.surface: Air holds mainly oxygen, nitrogen and one more gas to name.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the blank is the third most plentiful gas in air.
explanation.definitionFit: After nitrogen and oxygen, argon is the most abundant gas in the atmosphere, about one percent.

clue.text: Kitchen appliance made of wood by sink failing to start

indicators.note: failing to start means the opening letter is missing

blocks.note: teak is a hardwood
to settle is to sink down

explanation.surface: A kitchen fitting made of timber beside the sink that won't turn on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' looks like the kitchen basin, but it is the verb meaning settle.
explanation.definitionFit: A teakettle is a kettle for boiling water to make tea.

clue.text: Momentous, or alternatively heart-breaking?

indicators.note: alternatively means in another way, so the letters take a different arrangement

blocks.note: the word as letters to be rearranged
shattering means breaking into pieces

explanation.surface: Something huge, or perhaps just emotionally devastating?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart-breaking' reads as one word, but the hyphen hides two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth-shattering describes something of enormous importance, which is momentous.
